transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (Pinecrest Head Data), Rajiv Menon (Cloud Architect), Harper Lee (Security)

Summary (auto): quick POC scoping to decide deployed mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for Pinecrest's claims triage and document ingestion use case. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, data residency), benchmark plan, timelines, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SAML), and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a quick intro then dive into the POC scope. I'm Sophie, AE at Redwood. Marco is our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Lena Patel: hi Sophie, hi Marco, thanks, um, quick context, Pinecrest is moving to LLMs for claims triage, we have roughly 50k monthly active users hitting the API, some peaks during month-ends, and--
[00:30] Rajiv Menon: yup, and we're primarily on GCP, we run most infra in us-east4 and europe-west1 for residency. Security is huge, Harper's on for that.
[00:40] Harper Lee: yes, we need SOC2 plus EU data residency, and we use KMS for key management, also SAML SSO and RBAC for dev/stage/prod separation.
[00:55] Marco Alvarez: cool, that helps. quick clarifying q: are you thinking hosted first for a quick proof, or do you expect dedicated / private from day one?
[01:06] Lena Patel: we'd prefer hosted for speed, but our security team wants to know if Dedicated or Private is necessary because we have regulated PII in some payloads. so, basically decision criteria are compliance (SOC2, residency), predictable throughput, and cost target.
[01:22] Sophie Chen: totally makes sense. for Redwood, typical pattern is hosted to validate model/UX and then move to Dedicated if you need reserved capacity and stronger isolation; Private if you need VPC/on-prem for compliance. we'll scope the POC to show the tradeoffs.
[01:35] Rajiv Menon: can you explain the perf differences? our SLO target is p95 under 300ms on short prompts (~150 tokens) and sustained 200 QPS during peaks.
[01:48] Marco Alvarez: yep. so hosted gives you the fastest onboarding but multi-tenant underlying infra, we provide encryption at rest and in transit, SOC2, and optional encrypted request logging policies. latency is usually low but not guaranteed for reserved throughput. Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool — predictable p95 because you're not sharing capacity, and we can tune batching and KV cache for your workload shape. Private gives you the most control: VPC, customer KMS/HSM, and full network isolation.
[02:12] Marco Alvarez: there are tradeoffs: Dedicated costs more but gives consistent latency and throughput; Private adds ops overhead and longer lead times for deployment.
[02:25] Lena Patel: ok what about caching and long-context KV? we have cases with repeated prefixes from claim forms.
[02:33] Marco Alvarez: we do prefix caching and KV cache optimizations; that reduces token regen and cost. sometimes these are, uh, called prefix/kv or kv-cache, transcription sometimes shows KV chache, but yes we can configure TTLs per customer.
[02:48] Harper Lee: on the security side, we need logs for audit but logs cannot contain full PII. can Redwood redact or control logging?
[02:56] Sophie Chen: yes, we have log redaction and filtered audit logs, plus retention policies. we can also configure no-persist mode for sensitive routes.
[03:05] Rajiv Menon: regarding model choices, we need a mid-sized open model for most workloads, with fallback to a smaller quantized model for cost. can Redwood do model variants and automated fallback?
[03:18] Marco Alvarez: absolutely, routing policies allow fallback to quantized variants and region-based routing. for benchmark we usually test 2 models: the baseline (full-fp32 or 8-bit fine tuned) and a quantized variant (4-bit / int8), capture latency, token cost, and quality metrics (BLEU / ROUGE / custom evals).
[03:36] Lena Patel: quality metrics: we'll need false positive rate under 5% for triage and explainability for decisions. also we want model drift alerts.
[03:45] Marco Alvarez: we have quality monitoring and eval hooks; we can tie regressions to a prompt set and trigger alerts.
[03:52] Sophie Chen: ok let's propose a POC plan: 2 week hosted pilot to validate prompt set and quality, concurrent benchmark comparing hosted vs dedicated with your traffic replay, then decision to move to Dedicated if latency/cost need guarantees, or Private if compliance requires it.
[04:10] Rajiv Menon: timeline wise, how soon can we start? we have internal change freeze the week of 2026-07-04, so ideally the pilot starts by 2026-06-30.
[04:20] Marco Alvarez: we can start hosted immediately, I'll need traffic samples and API traces to create the load harness. for Dedicated, reserving 8xA100-80GB pool typically takes ~2 weeks provisioning lead time. Private on-prem will take longer, 4-8 weeks depending on network and KMS integration.
[04:38] Harper Lee: about encryption: we require customer-managed keys (bring your own key). can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[04:45] Sophie Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted we support an envelope encryption model with KMS integration for enterprise customers (we'll share the architecture diagram).
[04:57] Lena Patel: cost targets: we want cost per 1M tokens <$120 when amortized into our app; is that feasible?
[05:05] Marco Alvarez: depends on model and batching. with aggressive batching and KV cache on short prompts, we can get unit cost down; Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale. we'll run cost projection in the benchmark report.
[05:16] Rajiv Menon: can you also measure cold-start latency and token tail latency around 95/99 percentiles?
[05:23] Marco Alvarez: yep we'll capture p50/p95/p99, cold-start, and tail, and include concurrency profiles.
[05:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:35] Sophie Chen: quick note on telemetry: Redwood Console will give per-route token breakdowns, cost per model, and tracing hooks to link requests to logs.
[05:45] Harper Lee: SSO - we use Okta, SAML assertions and role-based access, can you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[05:52] Marco Alvarez: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning are supported; we'll include RBAC mapping templates.
[06:00] Lena Patel: what success criteria should we set for the POC so we can make a clear go/no-go decision?
[06:07] Sophie Chen: good q. proposed success criteria:
- Functional: model satisfies triage accuracy (FPR < 5%, precision/recall thresholds you define) for production prompt set.
- Performance: p95 < 300ms on 150-token prompts under 200 QPS sustained (or agree burst profile).
- Cost: cost projection below your threshold ($120 per 1M tokens amortized) on projected monthly volume.
- Security/Compliance: ability to meet SOC2, EU residency, KMS integration or Private deployment option.
[06:45] Rajiv Menon: ok, and what will the benchmark deliverables look like?
[06:49] Marco Alvarez: deliverables: benchmark results CSV (latency quantiles, throughput curves), cost model spreadsheet, quality evals on your labelled set, automation scripts, and suggested config (batching, KV TTLs, model quantization).
[07:03] Lena Patel: for the traffic profile, we'll supply a week of anonymized traces and a labelled sample of 2k prompts for quality testing.
[07:10] Rajiv Menon: for Dedicated sizing: what GPUs and how many? rough ballpark to begin capacity planning.
[07:16] Marco Alvarez: initial recommendation: 8xA100-80GB for baseline, scales up with concurrency. if you need lower cost per token on heavy workloads, we can propose mixed fleet with cheaper quantized nodes. we'll include a sizing table.
[07:28] Sophie Chen: note that Dedicated can be configured with autoscaling policies with reserved baseline and burst capacity; that helps with month-end peaks.
[07:36] Harper Lee: audit logs: retention 7 years? we can't keep PII in logs, but we need event-level audit.
[07:44] Marco Alvarez: we support configurable retention and can redact PII fields before logging. we'll share the audit flow.
[07:52] Lena Patel: any known limitations on private deployment for our on-prem data center? firewall/NAT rules?
[07:59] Marco Alvarez: Private requires a VPN or VPC peering plus open ports for control plane. on-prem install is more involved; we'll need network diagrams and an infra window. lead time is typically 4-8 weeks.
[08:12] Sophie Chen: ok next steps recap: we'll send security docs and SOC2, Marco will prepare the benchmark plan, and Rajiv will share traffic. can we lock a starting date 2026-06-30 for hosted pilot?
[08:24] Lena Patel: yes that's good if you can start then.
[08:27] Sophie Chen: great. any other questions?
[08:30] Harper Lee: one more — data residency: can hosted guarantee EU-only processing for some routes?
[08:36] Marco Alvarez: yes, region routing can enforce processing in europe-west1 and avoid cross-region egress; we'll document region-specific storage/processing.
[08:45] Rajiv Menon: will the logs and model artifacts remain within region?
[08:49] Sophie Chen: for Hosted we can enforce region residency for data at rest; for full guarantees we recommend Private with on-prem or VPC with restricted storage.
[08:58] Lena Patel: ok thanks, that helps.
[09:01] Sophie Chen: perfect — we'll send the items and schedule the benchmark kickoff. thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with small clarifications and interruptions; meeting ended ~15:58 UTC)

Recap / Action Items (auto):
- Sophie: send SOC2, security whitepaper, KMS integration docs, RBAC/SAML examples.
- Marco: benchmark plan, load harness, suggested model variants, and cost projection.
- Rajiv: sample traffic and labelled prompt set.

End of transcript.
